name: Logistics & 3PL
one_liner: Moving and storing goods for shippers through parcel, freight forwarding, warehousing and contract logistics, a density- and utilization-driven business.
how_it_makes_money: Parcel carriers charge per package based on weight, zone and speed, plus surcharges. Third-party logistics (3PL) providers earn fees for warehousing, fulfillment and value-added services, often under multi-year contracts. Freight forwarders and brokers are asset-light and earn a spread between what they charge shippers and pay carriers.
revenue_formula: Parcel revenue = packages per day × days × revenue per piece
Warehousing revenue = square feet or pallets × storage rate + orders handled × fulfillment fee
Broker/forwarder net revenue = shipments × (price charged − carrier cost)
cost_structure: Labor: drivers, warehouse staff; typically the largest cost
Purchased transportation: fees paid to third-party carriers
Fuel: largely passed through via fuel surcharges
Facilities: rent and depreciation of hubs and warehouses
Fleet and equipment, including aircraft for express players
margins: Asset-heavy parcel and express carriers typically earn high single to low double digit operating margins, while contract logistics and brokerage margins are thinner on revenue but asset-light. Network density, utilization and freight cycle drive the spread.

key_metrics.name: Revenue per piece
key_metrics.what: Average yield per package, driven by weight, zone and service mix.

key_metrics.name: Cost per piece
key_metrics.what: Unit cost; density is the key lever.

key_metrics.name: Packages per stop / stops per route
key_metrics.what: Last-mile density, the biggest driver of delivery cost.

key_metrics.name: Warehouse utilization
key_metrics.what: Share of capacity used, key to 3PL profitability.

key_metrics.name: On-time delivery rate
key_metrics.what: Service quality measure customers pay for.

key_metrics.name: Gross margin / net revenue per load
key_metrics.what: Spread earned by brokers and forwarders.

trends: Amazon's in-house logistics network competing with UPS and FedEx
Warehouse automation and robotics to offset labor costs
Nearshoring and supply chain diversification away from China
Freight market downcycle pressuring rates and volumes
Carriers shifting toward higher-margin volume over raw volume
Tariffs and changing de minimis rules affecting cross-border ecommerce
